title: Calegari and Louwsma, Immersed surfaces in the modular orbifold
body:
## The reference

Danny Calegari and Joel Louwsma, *Immersed surfaces in the modular orbifold*.

The journal, volume and year are not recorded here: the source in the author's
directory is a working draft, and the publication details were not in it. Whoever
has the published version should supersede this record with them.

## Why it is relevant

It contains the Stability Theorem, which is the proved case of the eventual
linearity of scl under stabilisation along a boundary curve, and the one concrete
piece of evidence that the unbounded winding obstructing the cut-and-glue approach
to rationality in surface groups may be tame rather than fatal.

It also proves a generalisation to hyperbolic (2,p,infinity)-orbifolds for every
p at least 3, and, via the central extension of PSL(2,Z) by the three-strand braid
group B_3, an analogous stability statement in B_3.

The conjecture that the theorem settles in this case originates in Calegari,
*Faces of the scl norm ball*, as Conjecture 3.16, where it was observed
experimentally that for many words w in the commutator subgroup of F_2, the
geodesics corresponding to [a,b]^n w on a hyperbolic once-punctured torus all
virtually bound immersed surfaces for sufficiently large n.
